British A Petition of the Trustees of the Mufem, Museum. being offered to be presented to the House;

The Lord horth, by His Majesty’s Command, acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends the fane to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read;

Setting forth, That, in the Second Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, the said Trustees represented to Parliament, that the Sum allowed for the Establishment and Support of the said Museum was reduced to a Capital of £.$0,000. Reduced Bank Annuities, the Dividend of which, amounting to£. 900, was, notwithstanding their utmost Attention to the forming their Establishment with Frugality, greatly insufficient for that Purpose; upon which Represen-tation, they obtained a Grant of a further Sum of £. 2,000; and, upon like Applications to Parliament, in the 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, and 14th Years of His present Majesty’s Reign, the said Trustees obtained Grants of the further Sum of £.2,000, each of the said Years, for the same Purpose; which Sums, together with the Produce of the said £. 30,000, are so far (pent, that what remains will not be nearly sufficient to defray the Charges of the next Year; and that it is with Concern that the Trustees apply to Parliament so soon after their last Grant; and they would not have made the Application, if several extraordinary Outgoings and Expences did not render it necessary: And therefore praying the House to grant them such further Support, towards enabling them to carry on the Execution of the Trust repoled in them by Parliament, for the general Benefit of Learning and useful Knowledge, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Ordered, That there be laid before this House an Account of the Money granted by Parliament for the Use of the British Museum, and of the Expenditure thereof.

Clerk’s Table i Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the first-mentioned Petition, Mr. John Lane, being examined, laid, That the Poor of the Parish of Saint. Paul, Covent Garden, are very numerous, and are supported and maintained at a great Expence, and that the present Workhouse is too small for their Reception; and that if the Petitioners were empowered to hire or purchase a Piece of Ground to build a more convenient Workhouse thereon, for the Reception, Maintenance, and Employment, of the Poor of the said Parish, under proper Regulations, the Poor would be much better managed and supported, and would also be maintained at a less Expence than they are at present.

In Support of the Allegations of the second-mentioned Petition, Mr. Lane informed your Committee,

That the Church-yard of the said Parish hath, from the Increase of the Inhabitants, and the Burials there, been found too small for the Interment of the Dead; and that it would be of great Benefit to the Inhabitants of the said Parish, if Part of the Ground, so to be hired or purchased for building a Workhouse upon, was permitted to be used and applied to the Purposes of a Burial Ground.

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act to enable Sir Nigel Grejley, Baronet, and Nigel Bowyer Grefley, Esquire, his Son, to make and maintain a navigable Cut, or Canal, from certain Coal Mines, in dale, to Newcastle under Lyne, in the County of j

without any Amendment: And also,

The Lords have passed a Bill, intituled, An Act to dissolve the Marriage of Robert Greene, Merchant, with Juliana Greene, otherwise Judge, his now Wife; and to enable him to marry again; and for other Purposes therein mentioned; to which the Lords desire the Concurrence of this House.

And then the Messengers withdrew.

The other Order of the Day being read;

Resolved, That this House will. Tomorrow Morning, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of granting a Reward to such Person or Persons, His Majesty’s Subjects, as shall discover a Northern Passage from Europe to the West and Southern Ocean of America, and also to such Persons as shall penetrate to the North Pole.

THE Hour, appointed for taking into Corifidera-tiort the Petition of Daniel Campbell, of Shawfield,- Esquire, complaining of the undue Election and Return of Andrew Stuart, Esquire, for the County of Lanerk, being come;

The House proceeded to the Appointment of a Seleffc Committee, to try and determine the Merits of the said Election and Return, according to the Directions of Two several Acts of Parliament, passed in the Tenth and Eleventh Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, (of the regulating the Trials of controverted Elections or Returns of Members to serve in Parliament.

The Serjeant at Arms was directed, by Mr. Speaker, to go with the Mace to the Places adjacent, and require the immediate Attendance of the Members oa the Bufinets of the House.

And he went accordingly.

And being returned;

The House was counted by Mr. Speakefr, and 128 Members being found to be present;

The Counsel and Agents on both Sides were called in to the Bar: The Clerk, appointed to attend the said Select Committee, attending also at the Bar,

And the Door of the House being locked, the Clerk was directed, by Mr. Speaker, to read the Order of the Day, for taking the said Petition into Consideration.

And the same being read accordingly;

The Box, containing the Names of all the Members, of the House, and sealed with Mr. Speaker’s Seal, was placed upon the Table; and the Seals being inspected by Mr. Speaker, the Attestation annexed to the Out-side of the said Box, signed by Mr. Speaker, purporting, " That the said Box was, on the 6th Day cff " April 1775, made up in his Presence, in the Manner directed by an Act, made in the Tenth Year of " the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, An Act to regulate the Trials of controverted Elections " or Returns of Members to serve in Parliament," was read.

And the Seals being broken, and the Box opened, the Attestation inclosed therein, and signed by the Clerk, purporting, " That the Names of all the Members were by him, in the Presence of the Speaker, " put into the said Box on the 6th Day of April " 1775," was read.

And the said Names, written on distinct Pieces of Papes, being all as near as might be of an equal Size, and rolled up in the same Manner, were, by the Clerk, takeh out of the said Box, and put in equal Numbers into SLt Glasses, placed on the Table for that Purpose, and were there shaken together; and then the Clerk publicly drew out of the said Six Glasses, alternately, the said Pieces of Paper, and delivered them to M -. Speaker, who fead the same to the House.

And the Names of Twenty Members, then present, were drawn, who were not objected to.

And the Name of Henry Dundas, Esquire, being drawn, the Counsel for the Sitting Member declared, that the said Member was intended to be nominated by the said Sitting Member; and the said Member having in his Place contented to such Nomination, and no Objection being made to his serving on the said Select Committee as such Nominee, hk Name was set aside.

A Petition of the several Owners and Occupiers of Mitford. Messuages, Tenements, Lands, and Hereditaments, within the Hundreds of Mitford and Launditch, in the County of Norfolk, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, was presented to the House, and read;

Setting forth. That the Petitioners have perused a Bill depending in the House, for the better Relief and Employment of the Poor within the said Hundreds; and that the said Bill contains many extraordinary Powers and Provisions; and that several of the Clauses therein contained will be injurious to the Properties of the Petitioners: And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by themselves or Counsel, against such Parts of the said Bill as may affect them; and that they may have such further and other Relief in the Premises, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee, to whom the Bill for the better Relief and Employment of the Poor, within the Hundreds of Mitford and Launditch, in the County of Norfolk, is committed; and that the Petitioners be heard, by themselves or Counsel, before the said Committee, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the said Committee, That they do admit Counsel to be heard, at the same Time, in favour of the said Bill, against the said Petition.

Mr. Whitworth reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Trustees, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, for putting in Execution several Acts of Parliament, of the 3d and 8th Years of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the First, and the 7th, 8th, 26th, and 29th Years of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the Second, for repairing the Highways from several Places in the said Acts mentioned, leading to Highgate and Hampstead, in

Rie County of Middlesex; and for making a new Road from the great Northern Road at to the Edg-

ware Road, near Paddington, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, of the 25th of April 1774, relative to Turnpike Bills, had not been complied with, owing to the Petitioners not having been acquainted with, the fame; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as' it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, the said Acts were read. And,

Mr. John Benson, Cicrk and Treasurer to the said Trustees, being examined, laid, That the Trustees have proceeded in the Execution of the said Acts, and have borrowed a considerable Sum of Money on the Credit of the Tolls, which has been laid out in repairing the Roads, and other the Purposes of the said Acts; and that there is stili due and owing’ the Sum of

£. 13,975 I2J. 4 d.which cannot be discharged, nor the said Roads effectually kept in Repair, unless the Terms of the Acts are further continued, and the Powers thereof altered and enlarged.

That the l olls are considerably decrealed, owing, as the Witness apprehends, to the making of the New City Road, and the Badness of the Street Pave-

ment, together with the present good State of the Pavement through the City; and the Witness also apprehends, that from the said Decrease, and the Difficulty of procuring Materials for the Repair of the Roads, it will be necessiiry to raile the Tolls.

The Witness further said, That the several Roads VOL. 35.

Widows* &c.

279

leading to Highgate Gatehouse and Hampjleaa, in the said Acts mentioned, are very inconvenient and dangerous to Persons travelling the same in the Night-time, being much infefted with Robbers, which might in a great Measure be prevented, and the Lives and Properties of Passengers rendered more secure, if the Trustees were empowered to watch and light the said Roads; and that it would also conduce to the Convenience of Passengers, and the Inhabitants of Houses on the Sides of the said Roads, if Power was given to water the fame.

Mr. Thomas Elwes confirmed the above Evidence.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to continue, and render more effectual, several Acts of Parliament, for repairing the Highways leading to Highgate Gatehouse and Hampstead, and other Roads in the said Acts mentioned, in the County of Middlesex; and also to continue, and render more effectual, an Act to enable the respective Trustees of the Turnpike Roads leading to Highgate Gatehouse and Hampstead, and from St. Giles's Pound to Kilbour Bridge, to make a new Road from the great Northern Road at ljlington, to the Edgware Road, near Paddington, lb far as the same is by the said Act directed to be under the Care and Management of the Trustees of the said first-mentioned Acts; and for watching, lighting, and watering, the said Roads: And that Mr. Whitworth and Mr. Pentcn do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

Mr. Wolfeley, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of granting a Reward to such Person or Persons, His Majesty’s Subjects, as shall discover a Northern Railage from Europe to the West and Southern Ocean of America, and also to such Persons as shall penetrate to the North Pole, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerks Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Discovery of a Northern Passage, from Europe to the West and Southern Ocean of America, upon any Meridian whatsoever, would be of great Benefit and Advantage to the Trade of this Kingdom.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, in order to encourage Adventurers to attempt the said Discovery, a public Reward should be given, not only to such Person or Persons as shall make a perfect Discovery of the said Passage, but also to the Owners of such Vessels as shall penetrate to the North Pole.

The said Resolutions being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Ordered, That a Bill be brought in, upon the said Resolutions: And that Mr. Wolfeley and Captain Luttrell do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

A Petition of George Walker, Esquire, Agent for the Island and Colony of Barba does, in the Behalf, and by Order, of the said Colony, being offered to be presented to the House;

The Lord North, by His Majesty’s Command, acquainted the House, that His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth. That the said Colony have made a considerable Progress in restoring a proper Depth of Water in the Harbour at the Bottom of Carlisle Bay, in the said Island, which they intend to perfect and preserve for the future, and to build convenient Wharfs, according to the original Plans and Estimate now ready to be produced to the House, a Work of great and general Utility to the Navigation of the British Empire, in as much as the said Island is the First Port for all Vessels going to the West Indies, from Europe, Africa, and the greater Part of North America-, and that the said Colony have expended, in the Prosecution of the said Work, the £. 5,000 formerly granted to them by Parliament for that Purpose, together with the annual Produce of certain Duties imposed for the same Use by their own Legislature, amounting to about 2,000 a Year, which Duties they have lately continued until the said Work shall be completed; and that the said Colony already find such Advantages from so much of the Plan as has been executed already, as to render them anxious to finilli it, but are unable to make any greater Exertions themselves: and being sensible that the flow Produce of the Tax is unequal to the Dispatch necessary to be made in completing the Moles intended to break off the Force of the Sea, and to keep out the Sand, even upon a Principle of Frugality, they have directed the Petitioner to make Application on their Behalf to the House, for some further Assistance in this public Undertaking: And therefore praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and to give to the said Colony such Relief and Assistance as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Ordered, That the Committee, who were appointed to review and consider the several Laws which concern the Relief and Settlement of the Poor, and the Laws relating to Vagrants, and also the State of the several Houses of Correction, within that Part of Great Britain called England, have Power to report their Opinion, from Time to Time, to the House.

Sir Cecil Wray reported from the Committee, who were appointed to review and consider the several Laws which concern the Relief and Settlement of the Poor, and the Laws relating to Vagrants, and also the State of the several Houses of Correction, within that Part of Great Britain called England; and to report the fame, with their Opinion thereupon, from Time to Time, to the House , that the Committee had considered the Matters to them referred j and had come to several Resolutions, which they had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz,

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Laws relating to the Poor, in that Part of Great Britain called England, are defective, and the good Purposes intended by them in many Respects prevented.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the present Method of regulating such Poor, in separate Parishes and Townships, is, in general, ineffectual for their proper Relief and Employment.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Money raised for the Relief of the Poor is a grievous, and, if no new Regulations are made, will be an encreasing, Burthen upon the Public.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a considerable Part of such Money is expended in supporting Litigations concerning Settlements.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the employing of the Infant and Able Poor, in such Works, as may be suited to their Strength and Capacity, will be very beneficial to this Kingdom.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That if the Disputes about Settlements and Removals of the Poor between one Parish, or Place, and another, in the same County, could be prevented, the great Expence attending such Litigations would be saved, the Poor would have an ealier Access to Places where they might find Employment, and would avoid the cruci and severe Treatment which they frequently re-

ceive from the contending Parishes during such Contest.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, if the Poor were to be maintained and employed at one general County Expence, those Disputes would in a great Measure be avoided, the Spirit and Intention of the Statute made in the 43d Year of the Reign of Queen Elizabeth would be promoted, and the Regulations and Provisions therein contained better inforced.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the establishing proper Houses and Buildings, at such Places in each County, as shall be bell situated for the Reception, Accommodation, and Employment, of the several poor and disorderly Persons proper to be lent thither, and for the Convenience of their being duly inspected and attended to, will be the moll eaty and effectual Method for relieving the impotent, and employing the able, Poor.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Care should be taken, in the providing and establishing of such Houses and Buildings, for properly classing and employing the several Persons admitted therein , for which Purpose, and in order to the establishing a System of good Regulations, it m^y be proper to inspect the several Bye-Laws, Rules, Regulations, and Ordinances, constituted in the several Houses of Industry and Public Workhouses established under special Acts of Parliament within this Kingdom.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, for the better Government of the said Houses, and carrying the intended Regulations into Execution, every Person having an Ellate of f. 100 per,

in England, and f. So per Annum, in Wales, shall be a

Governor of the Poor, for the County wherein he resides, provided such Estate, or One Half thereof, shall lie in such County; and that there shall be one General Meeting of the Governors for such County, on a Day and Place to be fixed; at which Meeting the y shall determine the Places where the Buildings before described shall be ere died, and also what Parishes shall return their Rates and Accounts, and have their Correspondence and Transactions with each of such Houses, according to their Situation and Vicinity, as near as conveniently may be; which Houses and Parishes shall be distinguished by the Name of the First, Second, (Ac. District; and that there shall be One Annual General Meeting of the Governors, at each of the said Houses, on feme certain Day to be fixed; and allb one Monthly Meeting of the said Governors, at the same Place, in the First Week in every Month, on a certain Day to be appointed by them; and that such Governors may, at their annual Meeting, elect, from Time to Time, such other Persons, residing in such County, and having Estates of such Value in the Dominions of Great Britain, as they shall think fit to be Governors, provided the Numbers so elected shall not exceed, at any one Time, a certain Number to be limited for each County, which Number shall, at such First General Meeting of the Governors at large, be distributed between the several Houses then to be fixed upon, as they shall think fit, and Election made accordingly.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Governors shall, at their Annual Meeting, appoint so many Persons, to be Guardians of the Poor, for the several Parishes, Townships, and Places, belonging to each House, as they shall think fit, having Estates of £. 25 per Annum or occupying Lands, (Ac. of f. 50 per Annum within such County j but no Person shall act as Guardian within any Parish, Township, or Place, whilst he shall be Churchwarden or Overseer of the Poor for the lame.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That

15 Geo. III. 11° 295

That there shall be aTreasurer and Clerk, and affo a Master and Matron, appointed by the said Governors, for each of the said Houses, at the First Meeting of the Governors after the said Houses shall be fit for the Reception of the Poor, and proper Salaries allowed to each of them.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the poor PeFfons, being lame, impotent, old, or blind, who are unable to work, or who cannot maintain themselves by their Labour, but stand in Need of Relief, shall be sent, from the respective Parishes and Places where they reside, to the said Houses, and there accomodated with every Thing suited to their several Necessities and Occasions; and such of them who shall be able to work, employed in Labour suited to their Strength and Capacity.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the orderly and industrious Poor, who, from accidental Sickness, Infirmities, or other unavoidable Causes, shall be rendered unable to maintain themselves and their Families by their Labour, may have temporary Relief from the Overseers of the Poor, within the several Parishes or Places where such Poor relide, with the Approbation of Two or more of the said Guardians, in such Manner as shall be most fui table to their Necessities.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That such of the Infant Poor, under the Age of Four Years, who have lost their Parents, or whole Parents are unable to maintain them, and shall be willing to part with them, may, by the Direction of Two or more of the said Guardians, be put out to nurse in that or fbme neighbouring Parish, until they shall be fit to receive Instruction,. and from that Time shall be sent to the House to which such Parish or Place shall belong, to be instructed in all necessary Duties, and employed in such Manner as shall be most suitable to their Age and Capacities.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That such of the Infant Poor, above the Age of Four Years, who have lost their Parents, or whose Parents are unable to maintain them, may, by the Direction of Two or more of the said Guardians, be sent to the House to which such Parish or Place shall belong, to be instructed in all necessary Duties, and employed as aforesaid.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That each of such Children respectively, when of proper Age to be placed out Apprentice, or to Service, shall be so placed out by the Governors, but if, at any Time, their Parents shall apply to the Governors, to have their Children returned before so placed out, and it shall be made appear to such Governors that the Parents are able to maintain them, the Governors shall order them to be returned.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Overseers of the Poor shall, in the last Week in every Month, send to the Treasurer of the House to which their Parish or Place belongs, according to the Regulations aforesaid, a true Account of all the Expences incurred relative to the Poor within such Parish or Place, for the Four Weeks next preceding the Week in which such Accounts shall be sent, after the feme respectively shall have been produced to Two or more of the said Guardians, and allowed by them.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Treasurer and Clerk shall make an Account of all Receipts and Payments within each Month, to be laid before the Governors at their Monthly Meetings; and shall also make, and lay before the Governors at such Meetings, Abstracts of the Expences ipeurred within the several Parishes by such Relief or Provisions aforesaid, pointing out the particular Ob-jed of such Expences, for the better Observation and Consideration of such Governors.

Vol. 35.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Governors, at their Monthly Meetings, shall in-- sped and examine all such Accounts, and if they find Cause to suspect that there has been Mismanagement, or any improper Behaviour therein, they may order the Persons concerned in such Transactions to appear before them at their next Monthly Meeting, provided the Place where such Matter arises shall not be more than Ten Miles from such House, and then and there enquire into the same upon Oath, and make such Order and Regulation therein as to them shall appear just and reasonable; if the Place shall exceed that Distance, the said Governors may grant an Order for the Persons so concerned to attend some neighbouring Justice of the Peace, at such Time and Place as he shall appoint, which shall be notified to the Persons so concerned, and such Justice shall, in like Manner, enquire into the fame, and make such Order and Regulation therein as to him shall seem fit.

Resolved, That it is the opinion of this Committee, That, for carrying the several Purposes aforesaid into Execution, Adefiinents shall be made, by Order of the Justices at their General Quarter Sessions of the Peace, upon every Parish, Township, and Place, within each County, according to the Proportion of Money raised within such Parishes and Places respectively, and applied on Account of the Poor,-upon a Medium of the Seven preceding Years; the Mode of ascertaining the Sums so raised to be particularly directed.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Accounts from each of such Houses shall be made up Quarterly, and laid before the Justices of the Peace for the County wherein such Houses are situate, at their General Quarter Sessions of the Peace, who shall in sped the fame, and make Orders for the Sums to be raised within the succeeding Quarter.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That no Parish, Township, or Place, shall be compelled to contribute more, in any One Year,-than such Average Sum.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, if it shall be made appear to the Justices, at their Court of General Quarter Sessions of the Peace, that a Reduction may be made in the said several Assessments, and that such Average Sum, for any Parish, Township, or Place, exceeds Four Shillings in the Pound, of the Annual Value of the Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, within such Parish, Township, or Place, upon a fair Valuation thereof made by Persons to be appointed by such Justices, at the Expence of such Parish, Township, or Place; then, and in that Cafe, such Court of Quarter Sessions shall, in all their. Orders for future Assessments, consider the Average. Sum, for such Parish, Township, or Place, at One Fifth Part of the Annual Value of such Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, so to be ascertained as aforesaid, instead of the Average Sum so first settled.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That each Riding in the County of York, and Division: of the County of Lincoln, and each District, City, Town, or Place, where more Parishes than one are incorporated for Relief of the Poor, by special Acts of Parliament, shall, with respect to all the Purposes of these intended Regulations, be considered as distinct Counties.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That these Regulations shall not take Effect in any County, until ordered by Two Parts in Three of the Persons qualified as aforesaid to be Governors, assembled at a Meeting to be held for that Purpose, after Two Months Notice thereof given in the public News Paper* circulated in that County, and signed by at lead Fifteen Persons so qualified.

Ordered, That the Matters, Governors, and Officers, having the Care and Direction of the several Houses of Industry or Public Workhouses established by Acts of Parliament, specially made for the Relief and Employment of the Poor, within that Part of Great Britain called England, do, on or before the 24th Day of June next, transmit to the Clerk of this House, in order to be by him laid before this House, an Account of the Number of Parishes in each District, City, Town, or Place, wherein any such House has been so established; the Money raised Annually by such Parishes, under such Acts of Parliament, within the lait Three Years, or since such Establishment, the Expences for their Buildings, and how and to what Purposes such Buildings are adapted; the Number of Poor contained therein, at Midsummer and Christmas in each Year, distinguishing the Able, the Aged, Infirm, and Infant, Poor, and also the Number in each of those Classes who died in each of such respective Houses within each of the said Years; how, and in what Labour or Manufacture, the Poor have been employed in each of such Houses, and the annual Amount of the Net Money earned by them; the annual Expences in maintaining them, distinguishing how much for Food, Cloathing, and Fuel, respectively, and also how much for Salaries and Allowances to Officers, and how much for other incidental Expences, within each of the said Years; and also the Amount of the Money paid or allowed within the said Parishes, in each of the said Years, on Account of the Poor who were not lent to the said Houses of Industry or Work-houses; likewise an Account of what Money has been borrowed by virtue of the said respective Acts, and how much thereof has been discharged within each of the said Years, and what Part thereof remains unpaid; and also Copies of all their Bye-Laws, Rules, Orders, and Regulations.

Ordered, That the Clerks of the Peace and Treasurers, or One of them, within the several Counties, Ridings, Divisions, Liberties, and Precincts, and the Town Clerks and Treasurers, or One of them, in the several Cities and Towns Corporate, within that Part of Great Britain called England, do lay before the Justices of the Peace, for each respective County, Riding, Division, Liberty, Precinct, City, and Town Corporate, holding Quarter Sessions of the Peace, at their next Midsummer General Quarter Sessions, an Account of the several Sums of Money expended within their respective Jurisdictions, for apprehending, and also in passing, of Vagrants, within the last Three Years, distinguishing each Year; and also how much Money has been expended in each of the said Years on Account of the several Houses of Correction, within their respective Jurisdictions; how many Persons have, in each of the said Years, been confined within such Houses of Correction, for Employment in Hard Labour and Correction; how, and in what Manner, such Persons have been employed, and what Net Money has been earned by' their Labour, within each of the said Years; and that the Governors, and other Persons having the Care or Management of the several Houses of Correction, do give ail Assistance and Information in their Power, in making up the said Accounts; and the Justices of the Peace, at their said Quarter Sessions, within their respective Jurilclidtions, are required to inspect and certify the same to this House; and that the said several Clerks of the Peace, Town Clerks, and Treasurers, or One of them, do immediately afterwards transmit such Accounts and Certificates to the Clerk of this-House, in order that the same may be by him laid before this House,

The other Order of the Day being read;

Plymouth A Petition of the Inhabitants of the Town of i^*bonr. mouth., and of the Merchants and Commanders of Ships and Vessels using the Port thereof, being offered to be presented to the House;

The Lord North, by His Majesty’s Command, acquainted the House, that His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth. That the Port of Plymouth is one of the principal Places in this Kingdom for building, harbouring, repairing, and fitting out, the Navy; and that there is, within the said Port, an Harbour, called Cat-watery which is of great Consequence to this Kingdom as a Place of Resort for small Ships of War, and Store Ships, and Transports used in his Majesty’s Service, as also of such other Ships as Sail toward the West, or come from thence; and that the said Harbour is Ihel-tered from the Main Sea by a Neck of Laud, called Hoe Stcrt, or Mount Bathe Banks of which were

formerly secured from the Incroachment of the Sea by Edge Stone Walls that are now in a ruinous Condition, and in great Danger, without timely Prevention, of being entirely destroyed; whereby the said Harbour would be rendered useless, and the Passage through the Sound would become difficult and dangerous; and that the said Edge Stone Walls appear to have been built in, or soon after, the Year 1637, by the Mayor and Commonalty of the Borough of , who were

enabled to defray the Expence thereof by a Grant from the Crown of certain Duties on Ships using the said Port, and the Members thereof, for the Term of Three Years, and of the Perpetual, Sole, and Exclusive, Privilege of ballasting all Ships and Vessels within the Sound and Harbour of Catwater and; which

Privilege hath ceased to belong to the said Mayor and Commonalty for the Space of Sixty Years and upwards, having been diverted out of that Body by Parliament, and granted for a long Term of Years, which is dill l'ubfifting, to a private Person, by an Act, passed in the 8th Year of the Reign of her late Majesty Queen Anne, for the deepening and cleansing of the said Harbour, the Repair of those Walls making no Part of the Consideration for which the said Privilege was conferred; so that they seem to have been Objects that (material as they were at that Time) escaped the Attention of the Legislature, which probably hath been the Cause of their Decay; and that, upon consulting able and experienced Workmen, it appears that the most effectual Method of securing the said Neck of Land, will be to erect fence Walls, agreeable to the Plan annexed to the Petition, marked N® 1; and that there is, within the said Port, a Pool of Water, called Sutton Pool, lying in the Bosom of the said Town of Plymouth, which is capable of being rendered, as it formerly was, of great Ule and Advantage, as well to His Majesty’s Ships, for their Supply of Provisions, as to all Merchants who have Occasion to bring up their Vessels to load or unload at the Custom House and other Quays lying within the said Town; and that some Years ago there flood a Mole at the Mouth or Entrance of the said Pool, which rendered the same much more safe and commodious for the Purposes aforesaid, than it is at present, which Mole is now in Ruins; by Means whereof the said Quays have been so much exposed, that they have incurred frequent Dangers, and arc greatly run to decay, and the Landing Place is become very unsuitable to an Harbour of such Importance; and that the Pool is likely to become wholy unserviceable for the Uses aforesaid, if due Care be not forthwith taken for preserving the fame; and that the said Mole was, till the Time of its Deftnnftion, the Property of the said Mayor and Commonalty; and Vot. 35.

was, as the said Quays and Landing Place (the Property likewise of the said Corporation) now are, kept in Repair by the said Mayor and Commonalty, by Means of certain Port Duties, but whether the said Mole was originally built at the Expence of the said Mayor and Commonalty, or at the Expence of the Public, doth not now certainly appear; and that the Amount of the said Duties have been very much lessened since the Establishment of a Royal Dock in Hamoaze, which has given a Check to, and very much reduced, the Trade of the said Port, by reason (it is imagined) of the Hazard of being impressed, to which it exposes Seamen retorting thither in the Merchants Service; and that the Fund arising from the said Duties is not now (if it ever was) a competent Provision for the building of the said Mole; and that if a neW and convenient Mole, agreeable to the Plan annexed to the Petition, marked N° 2, was erected in or near the Place of the old, it would not only restore the said Pool to its former Utility, but would likewise afford a safe Retreat in tempestuous Weather to Boats, Lighters, and Tenders, engaged in the Service of Government (particularly to those attendingHis Majesty’s Victualling Office) and probably to several Ships of War, as well as Merchant Ships, when driven from their Anchors in the Sound by such Winds as hinder them from running into Hamoaze-, and that the Corporation and Inhabitants of the said Borough are unable to bear the Expence of completing the said Works; and that, necessary as they are for a Port of such Consequence to this Kingdom, the same cannot be done without the Aid of Parliament: And therefore praying for such Relief and Assistance as to the House shall seem meet and re-quisite for an Undertaking so conducive to the Service of the Nation.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Lord Barrington, Sir Charles Hardy, 8cc.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker’s Chan*-ber; and have Power to fend for Persons, Papers, and Records; and all who come to the Committee are to have Voices.

Mr. Mackworth reported from the Committee, to

whom the Petition of the Vicar and Churchwardens of the Parish of Saint Leonard, Shoreditch, in the County of Middlesex, and of a great Number Of the Trustees appointed by an Act, passed in the last Session of Parliament, for Relief and Employment of the Poor within the said Parish, and divers other Purposes, as also of several other of the principal Inhabitants and Parishioners of the said Parish, was referred; That' the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the lame, asi it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the feme was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, the said Act: was read: And,

Mr. Humphrey Bache being examined, laid, That when the Trustees held their First Meeting under the Act, many Persons who had Freeholds in Houses met, but they were told they could not aft unless their Estates confided of Freehold Lands, or Ground Rents, and they were intimidated from acting, and threatened to be prosecuted if they did aft: And he further feid, that there are several Misnomers in the Names of the Trustees in the said Act; that Mr. s Name is in the Act fpclt Thorpe; that he was objected to, his Name not being spelt right; but that he has acted, though the Wit nets thinks it was at his Peril; and that Mr. Buffington's Name is in the Act spelt Bdfington.

Mr. John BaJJington being examined, said, That he spells his Name BaJJington; and that he has not acted as a Trudee for Three Months. And being asked,. Whether he was threatened, if he acted as a Trudee, by any Person ? he feid, Not in particular; but that he had heard that Gentlemen, whose Names were mif-spelt, were to be prosecuted if they acted; and that he conceived the Misnomer would subject him to the Penalty in the Act if he acted. And being asked. Whether he had not been with the Trustees to (urvey the Parish, to make Assessments within Three Months ? he feid. That he had been with them, and that he received a Summons to attend upon that Survey.

Mr. James Wood being examined, said, That in the Act his Name is written John; that he was intended to be a Trudee; that he had been threatened with an Action in case he acted as a Trudee; that he has been One of the Churchwardens of the Parish ever since Easier 1774; that there is a John Wood in the Parish, but that he does not aft as a Trudee, and that he should not choose to act when he is out of his Office.

Mr. Thomas Draper being examined, laid. That the said Witness James Wood was the Person intended to #be appointed a Trudee in the said Act.

Mr ~ Roberts, the Clerk to the Trustees, attended your Committee with the Books of Accounts of the Trustees. And being asked, Whether he has the Mi-16

mates of the Proceedings at< the Fird Meeting of the Trustees under the Act ? he said, That he has not nor did he ever fee them.

Mr. Humphrey Bache being examined, was asked,. What are the Hardships and inconvemencies that have arisen to the Parish from the said Act in the Execution of it ? he said. The appointing a Surveyor, with an Allowance‘of £. 4 per Centum, \olay out near £. 7,000, when a Man of the Fird Abilities and Character as a Builder offered tb do the feme at per;

that a very large Quantity of Bricks for building the Workhouse’was agreed' for with'a Person at a very great Charge without the Trustees giving any Notice for a Public Contraft.

That the Trustees passed the Accounts of a Churchwarden who went out of Office at Easier lad, and had received many Hundred Pounds of the Parishioners for obtaining the Act; and though the said Churchwarden had been repeatedly called upon to deliver up and adjust his Accounts with the Parish, yet he refilled or neglected so to do; and that an Order of Vedry was made to file a Bill in Chancery against him.

Mr. James Stewart being examined,-feid. That lie did, on the 19th of December lad, with Mr. James Wood, One of the present Churchwardens, apply to Mr. Roberts, the Clerk to the Trustees, deliring to look at the Minute Book of the Trustees; that he asked Mr. Roberts, If the Fird Minutes in the Books were Original Minutes ? who said, He never few the Fird Minutes; that he then desired a Copy of those Minutes, and ' also a Copy of Mr. Churchwarden Thompson's Accounts, upon paying for them, which he promised he should have; and that on the 17th of February lad, Mr. Wilkinson, the other Churchwarden, and the Witness, called upon the said Mr. Roberts for the said Copies, according to his Promile, when he declared to them. That he should not give Copies to any Body. That the Witness asked him, By whose Orders he made the Refufel ? when he feid. That it was by an Order of the Board of Trustees written in the Book. That the Witness then asked the Favour to see the written Order in the Book, which the Clerk refund. And upon the Witness being asked, Whether when he fird asked Mr. Roberts for such Copies, and for Leave to see the Books, Mr. Roberts did not give him for Answer, that he should apply to the Trustees ? he feid. That he did not remember Mr. Roberts said any such Thing; but that he told him, that> according to the Order, he could not shew the Books or give Copies without Leave from the Trustees; that he never did apply to the Trustees for that Purpose, nor does he know of any Refufel being made by the Trustees.

That on the nth of November lad a Vedry was assembled, pursuant to Notice given, in order to make a Rate for the Relief of the Poor of the said Parish, according to the Directions of the said Act, and that the Witness at that Meeting made Application to the Trustees then present to produce their Accounts, which the said Trustees refused; and that One of the Trustees then proposed the Sums necessary to be raised, but did not explain the Debts due from the Parish, and that the Witness did not apply to the Trustees at their Meeting as he apprehended he had no Right to have such Account.

Mr. Thomas Draper being further examined, feid. That in same of the Removal of any of the Trustees out of the Parish, or Insolvency of a Trudee, neither the Parishioners nor Trustees are empowered to elect Trustees in their Room; and that a Trudee becoming insolvent can aft as a Trullee notwithstanding his Insolvency, and that he apprehends it a great Mard-ship upon the Inhabitants of the Parish to be liable to an Action for the Rates, even (or so small a Sum as Ten Shillings, when a Power is °iven to lev'' the

Mr. Eden, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of the Importation of painted Earthen Ware, the Manufacture of Europe, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report, to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in ^t the Clerk’s Table: Where, the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That painted Earthen Ware, except Galley Tiles of the Manufacture of Europe, be permitted to be imported* to be sold in this Kingdom.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Duties payable.on the Importation of Earthen Ware, according to the Rate of Ten Pence the Pound Weight, do cease, determine, and be no longer paid.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, upon the Importation of all Earthen Ware, except India or China, not otherwise rated, there shall be paid, for the Old Subsidy, Ten Pounds Ten Shillings for every One hundred Pounds, according to the true Value thereof.

The feid Resolutions being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

A Petition of Thomas Howell, and of the several other Persons whose Names are thereunto subscribed, was, presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners are, and for a considerable Time last past have been, Inhabitants and Housekeepers within the Borough of Hindon, in the County of Wilts', 'and as such were duly entitled to, and have exercised and enjoyed, the Right and Franchise of voting in the Election of Burgesses, to serve in Parliament for the said Borough; and that, on the Eighth Day of March last, a Bill was brought into the House, to incapacitate the Petitioners, and several other Persons therein named, from voting at Elections of Members to serve in Parliament for the said Borough, or elsewhere, wherein the Petitioners were charged with being guilty of Bribery at the late Election at Hindon; and that the Petitioners, having been duly served with Copies of the said Bill, did attend the House, by their Counsel, to make their Defence to the Charges therein specified against them, and were put to very considerable Trouble, Expence, and Loss of Time, in preparing Instructions necessary for that Purpose, and great Numbers of the Petitioners were necessarily forced to attend the House, and brought up many Witnesses from Hindon, to prove their Innocence of the Matters laid to their Charge by the said Bill; and that the Bill, at the Third Reading thereof, was thrown out of the House; and the Petitioners observe, that a new Bill is brought in, to incapacitate the Petitioners, and certain other Persons therein named; and representing to the House, that as they have done nothing ft> obstrud or evade the ordinary Course of the Laws against Bribery and Corruption, and have always been forthcoming, and never attempted to prevent the Service of legal Process, they hope no new or extraordinary Mode of Prosecution or Punishment will be adopted against them, by which they may be deprived of the usual Advantages given them by Law in the ordinary Course of Trial; and the Petitioners suggest, that a Bill, tending to deprive any Subject of this Realm of his greatest and dearest Franchise, cannot be deemed otherwise than a Criminal Prosecution against such Subject, and that, being once put upon his Defence, he cannot legally be called again to answer the same Charge; and that the Petitioners have been put to to great and heavy an Expence, in defending themselves against the Charges contained in the said last Bill, that they are unable to defray the Expences of the necessary VY itnesses and Journeys to London, to prove their Innocence against this Second Prosecution: And therefore praying, That the said Bill mav not pass into a Law; and that they may be heard, Vol. 35.

by their Counsel, on the Matters contained in this their Petition, and may be admitted before each of them is put upon his separate Defence, to shew Cause why this Mode of Prosecution should not be adopted in the present same against the Petitioners.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table, until the Bill to incapacitate certain Persons, therein mentioned, from voting at Elections of Members to serve in Parliament; and for preventing Bribery and Corruption in the Election of Members to serve in Parliament, for the Borough of Hindon, in the County of Wilts, be read a Second Time; and that the Petitioners be then heard, by their Counsel, against the said Bill, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

A Petition of the several Persons whose Names are thereto subscribed, Inhabitants and Housekeepers within the Borough of Hindon, in the County of Wilts, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Right of voting for Members to serve in Parliament, for the said Borough, is, by the last Determination of the House, vested in the Inhabitants of the said Borough, who are Parishioners, Housekeepers, and not receiving Alms, of which Denomination are the Petitioners; and that the Petitioners observe, that a Bill is now depending, to incapacitate several Persons therein named from voting at Elections for Members to serve jn Parliament, and to alter the accustomed and usual Mode of voting in the said Borough; which, if passed into a Law, will essentially and materially ailed the Rights and Franchises of the Petitioners, against whom there is no Charge of Bribery or Corruption, and who hope that their Rights and Privileges will not be thereby altered or abridged: And therefore praying the House, That so much of the said Bill, as relates to change or alter the Right of voting for Members to serve in Parliament for the said Borough, may not pals into a Law; and that the Petitioners may be heard by their Counsel, against the said Bill.

A Petition of the several Persons whose Names are thereunto set and subscribed, was also presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That a Bill is brought in, to incapacitate certain Persons, therein mentioned, from voting at Elections of Members to serve in Parliament, and for the preventing of Bribery and Corruption in the Election of Members to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Hindon, in the county of ; and that, by the said Bill the Petitioners are declared to be disabled from giving any Vote at any Election, for the choosing a Member or Members to serve in Parliament, either for the said Borough of Hindon, or for any County, City, Town, Borough, or other Place, in Great Britain-, and that the Petitioners conceive themselves aggrieved by the said Bill, in being so incapacitated: And therefore praying. That they may be heard, by themselves or their Counsel, against so much of the said Bill as relates to their laid Incapacitations.

A Petition of John Nairn, Clerk, was also presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Pcti -tioner has been served with a Copy of a Bill depending before the House, to incapacitate the Petitioner, and certain other Persons therein named, from voting at Elections of Members to serve in Parliament, and for other Purposes therein mentioned; and that the Petitioner is greatly concerned to find himself included in the said Bill, as a Person guilty either of having been bribed and corrupted at the late Election of Members to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Hindon, or as having been concerned as Agent lor the Purpose of felling the Seats in Parliament for the said Borough, or as having been instrumental in effectuating such Sale, and, for all or feme of the said Offences, to be declared incapacitated and disabled from giving any Vote at any Election, for the choosing a Member or Members to serve in Parliament, either for the said Borough ot Hin-don, or for any County, City, Town, Borouch, or other ' 4 M ~ Place,

Election. Dukes, of the Borough of Hindon, in the County of Wilts, was also presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That, on the 8 th Day of March last, a Bill was brought into the House, to incapacitate the Petitioners, and other Persons therein named, from voting in the Choice of Members to serve in Parliament for the said Borough, or elsewhere within this Kingdom; and that the said Bill was, at the Third Reading thereof, thrown out of the House, and a new Bill ordered to be brought in, in which the Petitioners observe several Persons are omitted that were included in the first Bill, for the Purpose, as the Petitioners have been informed, of being admitted Evidences in Support of the Allegations of the Bill now depending; and that the Petitioners are privy to, and desirous of giving Evidence to the House of, very interesting and important Transactions, respecting the Matters contained in the said Bill, which, if discovered and given in Evidence, will tend effectually to invalidate the Testimony of one or more Persons interested in the first Bill, omitted in the present: And therefore praying, That their Names may be struck out of and omitted in the said now depending Bill, in order that they may be produced as Witnesses, and examined, for the Purposes aforesaid.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Fishfritfc Mr. Cooper, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of what Encouragements it may be proper to give to the Fisheries carried on from Great Britain and Ireland, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the following Bounties be allowed to certain Ships, of the Burthen of Fifty Tons, or upwards, employed

1 in the British Fishery on the Banks of

for a limited. Time, under certain Conditions and Limitations} that is to say; a Bounty of Forty Pounds each to Twenty-five such Ships that shall first arrive in feach Year in the Island of Newfoundland, with a Cargo of Fish, not less than 10,000 by Tale, catched on the Banks thereof; and shall, after landing the fame, proceed for and return with one Cargo of Fish more, at least, catched on the said Banks; and a Bounty . of Twenty Pounds each for One Hundred such Ships which shall next atrive at the said Island with a like Cargo, and shall afterwards proceed again to the said Banks, and return from thence in Manner before-mentioned; and a Bounty, of Ten Pounds each for another One Hundred of such Ships which shall next arrive at the said Island with a like Cargo, and shall afterwards proceed again to the said Banks, and return from thence in Manner before mentioned.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the following ’Bounties be allowed to Five Ship6 belonging to Great Britain,. Ireland, or the Isle of Man, employed in the Whale Fishery in the Gulph of Saint Lawrence, or on the Coasts of Labrador, Newfoundland, or in any Seas to the Southward of the Greenland Seas and Davis's Streights, for a limited Time, under certain Conditions and Limitations; that is to say; to the Vessel that shall arrive in each Year in any Port of Great Britain with the greatest Quantity of Oil, being the Produce of One or more Whale or Whales taken or killed by the Crew of such Vessel, a Bounty of Five hundred Pounds; to the Vessel that ’shall in like Manner arrive in the same Year with the next greatest Quantity of such Oil, a Bounty of Four hundred Pounds; to the Vessel that shall so arrive in the same Year with the next greatest Quantity of such Oil, a Bounty of Three hundred Pounds; to the Vessel that shall so arrive in the same Year with the next greatest Quantity of such Oil, a Bounty of Two hundred Pounds; to the Vessel that shall so arrive in Jhe same Year with the next greatest Quantity of such Oil, a Bounty of One hundred Pounds; the Oil so to be imported by each of the said Ships being the Produce of One Whale at the least.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Liberty granted by Law to import into this Kingdom, Duty free. Oil or Blubber, and Whale Fins, from Greenland, and from the Parts and Seas adjacent, apd from those of Newfoundland, and of any other of His Majesty’s Colonies and Plantations in America, in Ships belonging to Great Britain, be extended to Oil and Blubber or Fish, and to Whale Fins of Whales, catched by Ships belonging to Great Britain, in any Part of the Ocean; and that the like Liberty be

granted to His Majesty’s Subjects of Ireland and the Isle of Man.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the like Bounties, which are granted by an Act of the 1 ith Year of His present Majesty’s Reign, to -Ships fitted out from Great Britain or America for the Whale Fishery, to the Greenland Seas and Davis's Streights, be allowed, under Certain Restrictidhs, to Ships fitted out for that Purpose from the Kingdom of Ireland, and from the Isle of Man.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Duty payable upon the Importation of Seal Skins, catched by Vessels belonging to Great Britain, Ireland, or the Ife of Man, and fitted out from thence respectively, shall cease, and be no longer paid.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Power be given to His Majesty’s Subjects residing in Ireland, to ship and transjjort from thence to Newfoundland, or any Part of where the Fishery

now is or may hereafter be carried on, Provisions, Hooks, Lines, Netting, or other Tools or Implements, of the Product or Manufacture of Great Britain or Ireland, necessary for, and used in, the Fishery, by the Ships or Vessels carrying out the fame, and the Craft belonging to, and employed by such Ships in, the said Fishery.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committed, That the like Power be given to His Majesty’s Subjects residing in the Isle of Man, to transport from thence, for the same Purpose, the like Provisions, Tools, and Implements, of the Product or Manufacture of Great Britain, or the Isle of Man.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Clothing and Accoutrements necessary for His Majesty’s Forces, which are paid out of any of His Majesty’s Revenues arising in the Kingdom of Ireland, and are sent from thence upon His Majesty’s Service, be allowed to be exported from Ireland, to the Places where such Forces shall be so ordered to serve, under certain Restrictions and Limitations.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Bounty of Five Shillings per Hogshead be allowed upon all Flax Seed imported, from any Place whatsoever, into the Kingdom of Ireland, for a limited Time, and that such Bounty be paid out of any Monies arising from the Revenue under the Management of the Commissioners of the Customs in England.

The laid Resolutions being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Ordered, That a Bill, or Bills, be brought in, upon the said Resolutions: And that the Lord North, Mr. Jenkinson, Mr. Rigby, Mr. Ellis, Mr. Thomas Townshend, the Lord Clare, Lord George Germain, Mr. Conollv, Mr. Cooper, and General Irwin, do prepare, and bring in, die fame.

Iicharjfon’s A Petition of Edward Richardson, of Pimlico, in the Recovery parish

of Saint George, Hanover Square, being offered to Debts be presented to the House;

10 The Lord North, by His Majesty’s Command, ac-

kbe Crown, quainted the House, that His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House:

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioner, in the Year 1763, married Elizabeth Pinncck, Mother of Anna Catherine Pinnock, who died in the Year 1762, being then about Seven Years of Age; that the said Anna Catherine Pinnock was, by the Codicil of the Will of Edward Manning, Esquire, Agent for Prizes at Jamaica (who died in the Year 1756) entitled to the Sum of 2,500 Sterling, payable at the Age of 21 Years, which Sum, by . her Death, became escheated to His Majesty, in Bight

of His Prerogative; and that the said Edward ^fanning being, at the Time of his Death, indebted to the Crown in the Sum of £ 22,200 Sterling, for the Value of several Ships and their Cargoes, taken from the Enemy, and condemned as lawful Prizes, his Executors prevailed on the Lieutenant Governor of Jamaica to certify to the Lords of the Treasury, that the said Edward Mamung died insolvent; and that the Petitioner, being an Officer of His Majesty’s Customs, made a Discovery to the Lords of the Treasury, in the Year 1768, that the said Certificate, which was transmitted to their Lordships from Jamaica, was fraudulently obtained; and that the Estate and Effects of the said Edward Manning would amount to near £. 70,000 Sterling, which was more than sufficient to pay all his Debts and Legacies; and that the Petitioner is informed that the Lords of- the Treasury have it not in their Power to grant him a Recompence for the said Discovery adequate to the Service rendered the Public, and the Trouble and Expence he hath unavoidably incurred therein; And therefore praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and grant him such Relief therein, as shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine, and state to the House, the Matter of Fad contained in the said Petition:

And it is referred to Sir Charles Whitworth, Mr. Cooper, &c.: And they are to meet upon Monday Morning next, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker’s Chamber.

Antigallican A Petition of James Layman and William Stone, on Privateer. Behalf of themselves and others, Proprietors of the Antigallican Private Ship of War, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Proprietors fitted out the said Ship, at an Expence of £.10,453; and, on the 26th of December 1756, (lie made a lawful Capture of the Due de Penthievre, a French Ship from China, valued at £.335,000, which Prize was condemned at Gibraltar the 28 th of February following; and that, on the 2d of March 1757, the Antigallican and her Prize, being in the Port of Cadiz, the Spaniards, with Force and Violence, seized the said Prize, without any reasonable Ground for such Procedure; and that, after various Applications to the Spanijls Ministers for Redress, they, instead of relieving the Petitioners, ordered the Ship Antigallican to be also seized, which was accordingly done, on the nth of August following; and that the Petitioners have never received the lead Satisfaction for the Injury; and that His Majesty gave the Proprietors His Royal Word that the Petitioners should be relieved by an Article in the late Peace, and that Orders were given for that Purpose, which were, by some fetal Delay or Neglect, never complied with; and the Petitioners are well allured that Copies of such Orders, and other material Papers relative thereto, are now in the late Lord Egremons Office; and that the Petitioners apprehend, that the Proprietors, being men, have a Claim of Protection, both in their Li-

berty and Property, from that. Government which they contribute to- support, particularly as their same is a public Insult to the whole Nation: And therefore' praying the House, That they may be relieved in such.

Manner as the House shall fee proper.

A Motion was made, and the Question being put.

That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee; and that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the feme, as it shall appear to them, to the House;

It passed in the Negative.

A Petition of Thomas Howell, now a Prisoner in gate, by virtue of an Order of the House of Commons, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioner, having been examined before a Committee of the whole House, relative to a Bill to incapacitate certain Persons therein mentioned from voting at Elections of Members to serve in Parliament, and for preventing Bribery and Corruption in the Election of Members to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Hindon, in the County of , touching the Absence of Thomas Spencer and John Two Persons who were ordered to attend the House, did, on such Examination, partly through Ignorance, trot rightly understanding feme of the Questions put to the Petitioner, and partly through Fear (the Petitioner not having been used to give Evidence before so great an Assembly) prevaricate in giving his Evidence; and that the Gaol of Newgate is so full of Criminals that the Petitioner cannot have even a Bed to lie on, and, from the Unwholesomenels of the Place, his Life is in great Danger, and the Petitioner hadi a Wife and several small Children dependent entirely on the Petitioner’s daily Labour: And therefore praying

the House to take the above Premises into Consideration, and grant the Petitioner his Discharge from the said Gaol o i Newgate (the Petitioner being willing and

desirous to alk Pardon, at the Bar of the House, for such his Offence, and sincerely promising never tp offend in the like or any other same for the future) or

Maii. A. 1775-

if it should be deemed necessary to prolong the Punishment of the Petitioner (which he hopes will be thought to have been already sufficient) that he may be Ordered-to be discharged from the said Gaol of Newgate, and sent to some more wholesome Prison, or that he may have such further or other Relief as to the House shall seem just.

Ordered, That Thomas Howell, committed by this House to His Majesty’s Gaol at for having

grolsly prevaricated in giving Evidence before a Committee of this House, be discharged from his Confinement there j and be, for his laid Offence, committed tq the Prison of the Gatehqufe; and that Mr. Speaker 49 issue his Warrants accordingly.

Resolved, That it. is the Opinion of this Committee,

That a Sum, not exceeding Five thousand Pounds be granted to His Majesty, to enable His Majesty to assist the Inhabitants of the Island of Barbadoes in defraying the Expence of cleansing the Channel, repairing the Mole, and rendering the Harbour there more fafeand commodious.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee*

That the Sum of One thousand Six hundred and Eighty-four Pounds Fifteen Shillings and Ten Pence, be granted to His Majesty, to make good the like Sum, which, has been paid to several Persons, as a Compenfetion, and in full Satisfaction, of their Losses and Expences incurred, pursuant to several Orders of Council, for preventing the spreading of the infectious Distemper amongst the Horned Cattle.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That a Sum, not exceeding Five hundred and Fifty Pounds, be granted to His Majesty, out of the Monies that have been, or shall be, paid into the Receipt of the Exchequer, on Account or the Sale of French Prizes taken before the Declaration of the late War, to be paid to Mr. Edward Richardson, or his Assigns, in Reward and full Satisfaction for the Information and Assistance given by him in the Discovery of the Estate and Effects of the late Mr. Edward Manning, one of the Agents for the Sale of the said Prizes in the Island of Jamaica.

A Petition of the Merchants, principal Tradesmen, Shopkeepers, and Manufacturers of Cutlery Wares, in Sheffield, in the County of York, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf of themselves and the rest of the Inhabitants of the said Town, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That, during the late Scarcity of the Gold Coin, of proper Weight and Quality, in the said Town and Places adjacent, occasioned by the Diminution thereof, the Silver Coin, which, before such Diminution, had been found fufli-cient for Change, became greatly insufficient to supply the Want of good Gold Coin for the necessary Purposes of the Trade, and therefore Two principal Banks were let up in the said Town for the Purpose of supplying the Inhabitants with Calli, and for negotiating Bills of Exchange, by Persons of unquestionable Capital and Credit, who deviled a Method of issuing out their Notes for One Guinea, Half a Guinea, and Five Shillings and Three Pence each, payable to the Bearer on Demand; which Notes were approved of, and received in Payment, by the Inhabitants, and were duly honoured by the Drawers, and were found to be of great Utility during the Scarcity of good Gold Coin; and that afterwards some inferior Shopkeepers and Retailers took upon themselves to issue Notes for is. 6 d.3 s.3*. 6 d.and 5J. 3 merely to answer a

self-interested Purpose, which they had Opportunities of enforcing upon the Inhabitants, in lieu of Silver Change; and although such smaller Notes passed current, yet the poorer Sort of Workmen, who were under the Necessity of taking them for their Wages, having no' regular Method of keeping and preserving such Notes, frequently by* MistakeHw*. Accident loft them, or they became destroyed, torn, or defaced, so that the Owners foftained great - Losses; and that, notwithstanding the said Two principal' Banks have declined issuing the said smaller Notes, and are paying off such as are outstanding, being now fumished with a sufficient Quantity of good Gold Coin, yet there is a very great Circulation of small Notes, which are daily issued out by a Person whom the Petitioners have Realbn to believe does not issue such Notes for the public Benefit, but for Purposes before observed; and the Petitioners have great Realbn to apprehend most Part of the‘Silver Coin, iVhich, in Consequence of the Commerce of the said Town, would circulate there, is with-held or 'lent away to a great Distance, to prevent the Inhabitants being supplied with the lame, the more effectually to enforce the Currency of such small Notes, which has produced a Scarcity of Silver Coin never known in the said Town; and' talfing Notice of the Bill to restrain the Negotiation of Tip-miffory Notes and Inland Bills of Exchange, under a limited Sum, within that Part of Great Britain called England; and alledging, that if the said Bill pstfles into a Law it will be of great Advantage' to the Trade and

Manufacture of the said Town,. and-prevent the In-

jdries frequently sustained through the accidental -Losses of 'such Notes, or by the tearing, defacing, and Deftfuftion, thereof: And therefore praying, That the said Bill may pafi into a Law, under such Provisions and Regulations as to the House shall seem meet; ‘ .

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the 18

That Books be opened, at the Bank of England, on the 8th Day of this Instant May, for receiving such Subscription and Consent as aforesaid; and that no Person or Persons, Bodies Politic or Corporate, be admitted to subscribe, or signify his, her, or their. Con-lent, for any Sum or Sums, amounting in the Whole to more than Twenty thousand Pounds, or to less than One hundred Pounds Principal or Capital Stock.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards raising the Supply granted to His Majesty, there be issued and applied the Sum of One Million Nine hundred and Fifteen thousand Five hundred and Fifty-two Pounds Sixteen Shillings and Eleven Pence Three Farthings, out of such Monies as shall or may arise of the Surplufes, Excesses, or Overplus Monies, and other Revenues, composing the Fund, commonly called the Sinking Fund.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards raising the Supply granted to His Majesty, the Sum of One Million Two hundred and Fifty thousand Pounds be raised by Loans or Exchequer Bills, to be charged upon the First Aids to be granted in the next Session of Parliament, and such Exchequer Bills, if not discharged, with Interest thereupon, on or before the 5th Day of April 1776, to be exchanged and received in Payment, in such Manner as Exchequer Bills have usually been exchanged and received in Payment.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Sum, not exceeding Fifteen thousand Pounds, out of such Monies as remain in the Receipt of the Exchequer, and that shall be paid in there on or before the 5th Day of April 1776, of the Produce of all or any of the Duties and Revenues, which, by any Act or Acts of Parliament, have been directed to be referred for the Disposition of Parliament, towards defraying the necessary Expences of defending, protesting, and securing, the British Colonies and Plantations in America, be applied towards making good such Part of the Supply as hath been granted to His Majesty, for maintaining His Majesty’s Forces and Garrisons in the Plantations, and for Provisions for the Forces in North America, Nova Scotia, Newfoundland, and the Ceded Islands, for the Year 1775.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That such of the Monies as shall be paid into the Receipt of the Exchequer, after the 5 th Day of April 1775, and on or before the 5th Day of April 1776, of the Produce of the Duties charged by Two Acts, made in the Fifth and Fourteenth Years of His present Majesty’s Reign, upon the Importation and Exportation of Gum Senega and Gum Arabic, be applied towards making good the Supply granted to His Majesty.
